headline: Russian overnight strikes hit Kryvyi Rih steelworks, Odessa port cargo vessels, substations
dek: Russia carried out large-scale overnight strikes: country's largest steelworks in Kryvyi Rih (ArcelorMittal; had suspended ops in September after ballistic strikes), vessels using Odessa port, electricity substation in Zhytomyr, another steel plant in Zaporizhzhia, a vehicle-repair plant in Lutsk,…
sources: TRT World, citing Russian Defence Ministry; Moscow mayor Sobyanin; Rosaviatsiya
fault_line: Ukraine shuts Moscow's skies; Russia hits steel, ports and power — who breaks first in the infrastructure war?

sections.what_happened: Russia carried out large-scale overnight strikes: country's largest steelworks in Kryvyi Rih (ArcelorMittal; had suspended ops in September after ballistic strikes), vessels using Odessa port, electricity substation in Zhytomyr, another steel plant in Zaporizhzhia, a vehicle-repair plant in Lutsk, substation in Ternopil, and a cargo vessel south of Odessa alleged to carry military/dual-use cargo. Sobyanin: 195 Ukrainian drones intercepted toward Moscow since midnight; Moscow's 4 airports closed ~midnight–7am Oct 17; Agentstvo: Moscow airports closed 101 hours in first 14 days of October vs 46 in all of September.
sections.what_verified: Multiple outlets (Kyiv Post, NV, Geopost, AviNews) confirm the Moscow drone wave and airport closures; infrastructure targeting fits both sides' stated strategies.
sections.what_disputed: Strike damage claims are Russian MoD assertions; Ukrainian confirmation of specific damage not yet checked; cargo-vessel 'military supplies' claim is Moscow's allegation.
sections.why_matters: The war of infrastructure, both directions: 101 hours of closed Moscow airports vs burning steelworks — the cost ledger, not the flag.
sections.context: Background: Russia/Ukraine — NEW (missed by prior scans): Russian overnight strikes hit Kryvyi Rih steelworks, Odessa port cargo vessels, substations
